Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. Attached is AzureBank's first-pass DPA redline (see "AzureBank_DPA_Redline_R1.docx") and a short PDF with questions about cross-border transfers and SCCs. Our privacy team flagged three items that we need to close before legal ops can route to procurement:

- Subprocessor list & notice window — AzureBank typically requires a 14-day advance notice + ability to object for critical processors.
- Data transfer mechanism — want confirmation Redwood will adopt EU SCCs (latest 2021 clauses) and a statement about onward transfers.
- Audit and compliance evidence — SOC 2 Type II report and logs retention details.

Can you have your privacy counsel review and come back with suggested language? If possible, we'd like to get to a countersign (DocuSign) by end of next week.

Also attaching an exported subprocessor CSV for your reference (we mapped the high-risk processors we expect).

Thanks —

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: AzureBank DPA redlines and SCC questions (Round 1)

Folks — reviewed AzureBank's round-1 redline and their SCC questions. I’ve annotated the doc and flagged the following items as blockers (priority order):

1) Subprocessors / notice & objection (Clause 3.2–3.4)
   - AzureBank requests 14-day notice + objection right for "critical" subprocessors. Our standard is 30-day notice for material changes with an option to pause provisioning for legitimate security concerns. Recommend we offer: 21-day notice + escalation with a joint remediation plan. If AzureBank insists on a 14-day window, propose limiting objection to predefined categories (e.g., subprocessors that process PAN/PII) rather than a blanket right.

2) Data transfers & SCCs (Clause 5)
   - We can accept incorporation of the EU SCCs, but need to append our technical and organizational measures (TOMs) as an annex and limit obligations on onward transfers to those reasonably necessary for the Service. Counsel suggests adding a sentence: "Supplier shall implement the Standard Contractual Clauses (EU) where applicable; Supplier shall only onward transfer Customer Personal Data to subprocessors where lawful and pursuant to the SCCs and Supplier's documented TOMs."

3) Audit rights & evidence (Clause 7)
   - AzureBank asks for on-site audits; propose remote evidence-first approach: provide SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summaries, and scoped log extracts. Offer up to one on-site audit per 24 months, subject to NDAs and cost-sharing for travel.

4) Liability cap and indemnities (Clause 9)
   - AzureBank increases cap to 2x fees; recommend preserving our standard cap (12 months of fees) but agree to carve-outs for gross negligence and breaches of confidentiality.

5) Incident notification timing (Clause 8)
   - Recommend keeping our contractual 72-hour notification, with ongoing updates as incident response progresses.

Deliverables: I attached an annotated redline (see attachments) and a proposed counter-draft for the SCC paragraph for Karthik to review. If we can agree to 21-day notice + SCC annex, we should be able to get to a countersignable DPA in round 2.

Marissa Cole
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: AzureBank DPA redlines and SCC questions (Round 1)

Nice summary Marissa — a couple of operational tweaks from procurement/legal ops perspective:

- Subprocessor timeline: prefer 21-day notice as Marissa suggested. We'll prepare a short explanatory note and a limited subprocessor registry to publish post-signature (we should request a carve-out allowing immediate notification for emergency security fixes).
- SCCs: we will accept incorporation but must keep our TOMs annex non-contractual in the DPA to avoid duplicative warranties; instead, reference a living security controls doc & provide snapshot at signing.
- Audit: agree to remote evidence-first plus one in-person per 24 months with cost sharing.
- Execution: propose we provide a countersigned DPA via DocuSign once we resolve the subprocessor language. I'll prepare the round-2 counter draft and a short cover note for Katherine outlining changes (we should be transparent about the 21-day notice compromise).

Action items:
1) Marissa — please convert the SCC suggested language into DPA redline form (I can merge and run final pass).
2) Neha — pull the latest SOC 2 Type II report and the up-to-date subprocessor registry export for attachment.

If we can get Marissa's redline back by EOD PST today, I’ll send to Katherine with a proposed DocuSign route and target countersign by Friday.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy Ops, Redwood Inference
